operations.name: Saw – Cut Bright-Bar Blanks
operations.setup_note: Clamp certified bright bar against the saw length stop and cut individual blanks, retaining facing allowance at both ends.

operations.name: CNC Turn – First End
operations.setup_note: Grip the left thread-end stock in bored jaws and support the projecting blank with a steady rest on unmachined stock clear of the journal cut. Machine the right end and finish F07 to establish datum A, using the right face as a shop axial reference rather than an additional drawing datum.

operations.name: CNC Turn – Second End
operations.setup_note: Reverse into bored soft jaws on finished F07, seat the right face against an axial stop, and indicate datum A; face the left end, create the permissible F02 center, and engage live-tailstock support. Run the reduced-diameter rough and finish profile in this loading, blending F06 during taper finishing and cutting F01 before external threading.

operations.name: Production Deburr / Clean
operations.setup_note: Place fully machined pins in a padded production nest for one fast pass removing residual thread-start and thread-exit burrs not eliminated by the lathe chamfers. Remove chips and cutting-fluid residue without polishing the taper or altering the specified bond-preparation finish.

operations.name: Batch Phosphate / Green Color Coding
operations.setup_note: Load the fully machined lot on the batch-line carrier using nonfunctional contact locations; provisionally protect the threads and gaged taper pending approval of PS-119.0 coverage requirements. Plan all 100 pieces as one line load, including specification-required embrittlement relief and localized green end-face color coding within the same line operation.

operations.name: Final Shop-Floor Gauge Inspection
operations.setup_note: Locate the finished pin from datum A in the dedicated gauge fixture and use production snap, thread plug/ring, and runout gauges under the approved sampling plan. Include taper bluing in the SAE J491a master gage for at least 60% properly distributed contact, together with coating and green color-code acceptance.

clarifications.question: Which process variant is ordered: part 043840 or part 043841?
clarifications.suggested_default: Plan part 043840, processed as shown; do not apply the unavailable PS-135.18 requirements for part 043841.

clarifications.question: Where are the three .020-inch × 45-degree chamfers represented by F08 located?
Can you provide the governing PS-119.0 phosphate-coating specification?
clarifications.suggested_default: For planning only, use the in-house phosphate line with threads and the gaged taper masked; include any required embrittlement relief within that line operation. Confirm coverage, dimensional allowance, and acceptance requirements before production.

clarifications.question: What preparation process is required by the 'BOND PREP THIS AREA ALL AROUND' callout on F07?
clarifications.suggested_default: For the as-shown 043840 variant, retain the specified 125-microinch machined finish over the indicated circumferential band without adding an unspecified abrasive or chemical preparation.

assumptions.text: The governing linear dimensions and GD&T values stored in fields named *_mm are inch values and must be multiplied by 25.4 downstream; angles and taper ratios are not converted as lengths. The envelope is approximately 205.105 mm maximum length and 49.657 mm maximum diameter, and the 50/125 finish callouts are microinches.

Use an approved stress-proof bright-bar material option with certification of at least 100,000 psi yield strength. No additional heat treatment is specified, and the 30–38 HRC condition associated with alloy alternatives is not imposed on this selected option; incoming HRC remains unknown.

Certified 50 mm bright bar is assumed commercially available. A 210 mm sawn blank provides approximately 4.9 mm allowance beyond the maximum finished length, and the main journal requires only a cleanup skim, not a rough-turning pass.
Part 043840 processed as shown is the provisional variant. PS-135.18 processing is not inferred for part 043841.
F01 uses the canonical main-view relief definition. The optional-detail limits are alternative-design requirements and are not applied cumulatively.

F02 is placed at the left end as a permissible retained manufacturing center. The first setup uses a steady rest, and the second uses this center for tailstock support; no third lathe setup or additional drawing datum is introduced.

The separate reduced-diameter roughing blocks belong to one consolidated canned profile cycle and do not each remove the full blank volume. F06 is physically produced by the taper finish profile rather than a separate radius operation, as required by the organizational corrections.

F08's 3X chamfers are provisionally retained as a grouped right-end chamfer step because the supplied feature lists +X access. Their actual locations require confirmation; no spatial pattern or additional chamfer feature is invented.

The .578-inch drilled hole is the specified preparation for F09, not a separate precision bore. Rough/finish boring, reaming, and honing are omitted because no precision cylindrical bore is called out; pilot drilling and deep-hole peck drilling are unnecessary for this approximately 14.68 mm diameter, 31.75 mm deep hole.

Center/spot drilling precedes drilling, and the threaded-hole entry chamfer precedes tapping so tapping is last in its hole sequence. The external lead-in chamfer likewise precedes thread cutting; one fast bench pass is retained for residual threading burrs.

Part-off is omitted because blanks are individually sawn and both ends are faced. The preloaded milling sequence is inapplicable because there are no prismatic features; no forging, heat treatment, grinding, intermediate inspection, CMM layout, or gauge-fabrication operations are added.

Surface cleaning, masking, phosphate processing, unmasking, and localized green identification are consolidated within the in-house batch-line operation. Any specification-required cure or embrittlement relief remains internal to that operation rather than a separate route gate.

Coating inspection and the specified taper-contact check are consolidated into the single final manual gauge gate. Inspection and temporary masking do not physically produce drawing features and therefore have empty target-feature lists.
